extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, agents, attorneys) involved in ex parte appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural/content requirements for amendments, affidavits/evidence, advisory actions, appeal conferences, and preparation and content of the examiner's answer in ex parte patent appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments on appeal (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new amendment must be submitted in a separate paper. Entry of a new amendment in an application on appeal is not a matter of right. The entry of an amendment submitted in an application on appeal is governed by 37 CFR 41.33, not 37 CFR 1.116.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments filed after the filing of a notice of appeal but prior to the date of filing a brief may be admitted only under the limited conditions set forth in 37 CFR 41.33(a). Amendments filed on or after the date of filing a brief are governed by stricter rules (see separate rubrics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted amendments after notice of appeal but before filing brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed after the filing of a notice of appeal, but prior to the date of filing a brief, may be admitted only to: (A) cancel claims; (B) comply with any requirement of form expressly set forth in a previous action; (C) present rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal; or (D) amend the specification or claims upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the amendment is necessary and was not earlier presented. See 37 CFR 41.33(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner denies entry of such an amendment, use form PTOL-303 to notify applicant of the non-entry and the reason. If an amendment clearly places the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter the amendment and allow the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted amendments after filing of an appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed on or after the date of filing a brief pursuant to 37 CFR 41.37 may be admitted only to: (A) cancel claims, where such cancellation does not affect the scope of any other pending claim in the proceeding; or (B) rewrite dependent claims into independent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewriting dependent claims into independent form includes (A) rewriting a dependent claim in independent form by adding the limitations of the parent claim(s), and (B) rewriting an independent claim to incorporate all subject matter of a dependent claim, canceling the dependent claim, and modifying dependency of other claims as needed. If entry is denied after filing a brief, use PTOL-304 to notify applicant and state reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of amendments filed same date as notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment, affidavit or other evidence filed after the mailing of a final Office action and on the same date as the notice of appeal will be treated by the Office as being filed prior to the notice of appeal and treated under 37 CFR 1.116. Any amendment, affidavit or other evidence filed after the mailing of a non-final Office action and on the same date as the notice of appeal will be treated as being filed prior to the notice of appeal and treated under 37 CFR 1.111.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware that same-day filings may be governed by different regulatory provisions depending on whether the prior Office action was final or non-final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/other evidence filed after notice of appeal (before brief) — admission criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or other evidence submitted after the date of filing a notice of appeal, but prior to the date of filing a brief, may be admitted if the examiner determines that: (A) the affidavits or other evidence overcomes all rejections under appeal; and (B) a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the affidavit or other evidence is necessary and was not earlier presented has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner denies entry of such an affidavit or other evidence, the examiner should use form PTOL-303 to notify the applicant of the non-entry and the reason. If the affidavit or other evidence clearly places the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter it and allow the application. Except as noted, affidavits or other evidence filed after the date of filing a notice of appeal will not be admitted except as permitted by 37 CFR 41.39(b)(1), 41.50(a)(2)(i) and 41.50(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of amendments/evidence after jurisdiction passes to the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment, affidavit or other evidence received after jurisdiction has passed to the Board should not be considered by the examiner unless remanded or returned by the Board for such purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 1210 and 1211.02 for procedures. Examiners must not consider such items absent Board remand/return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Action Before the Filing of an Appeal Brief (PTOL-303) — required notice content
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment/affidavit/evidence filed after a final rejection but prior to or on same day as a Notice of Appeal fails to place the application in condition for allowance, the advisory action must tell applicant to timely file one of: (1) an amendment/affidavit/evidence placing the application in condition for allowance; (2) a Notice of Appeal (with fee) in compliance with 37 CFR 41.31; or (3) a Request for Continued Examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The advisory action must set the applicable reply periods, note extension options under 37 CFR 1.136(a), and warn about earned patent term adjustment consequences for late replies. Use PTOL-303 form language when denying entry and explaining reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Action After the Filing of an Appeal Brief (PTOL-304) — required notice content
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment is filed on or after the date of filing a brief, advisory action must explain why the proposed amendment(s) will not be entered (e.g., they raise new issues requiring further search, raise new matter, do not place the application in better form for appeal, or present additional claims without cancelling corresponding finally rejected claims), or cite non-compliance with 37 CFR 1.121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PTOL-304 when denying entry post-brief and provide clear explanations of the specific reason(s) for non-entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duties when an amendment would be entered
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner indicates in an advisory action that an amendment would be entered, it is imperative for the examiner to also state how the individual rejection(s) set forth in the final Office action will be impacted by the entry of the amendment except where an amendment merely cancels claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner determines that an amendment clearly places the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter and allow the application. Examiners must respond to all amendments filed after appeal has been taken and prior to termination of the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: New ground of rejection in examiner's answer — appellant options and time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner's answer may include a new ground of rejection. If so, appellant must within two months from the date of the examiner's answer exercise one of two options to avoid sua sponte dismissal as to claims subject to the new ground: (1) reopen prosecution by filing a reply under § 1.111 with or without amendment or evidence relevant to the new ground (treated as request to withdraw the appeal); or (2) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief addressing each new ground (no amendment or evidence allowed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any reply brief filed to maintain the appeal must address each new ground as set forth in § 41.37(c)(1)(vii) and follow brief requirements. If a reply brief is accompanied by any amendment/evidence it will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution. Extensions of time under § 1.136(a) are not applicable to the two-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal conference requirement and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal conference is mandatory in all cases in which an acceptable brief has been filed, unless the examiner charged with preparing the examiner's answer concludes appeal should not go forward and the supervisory patent examiner (SPE) approves reopening prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should include (1) the examiner preparing the answer, (2) an SPE, and (3) a conferee examiner with sufficient experience. During the conference, consider dropping cumulative art rejections and eliminating technical rejections of doubtful value. If an appeal conference is held, the examiner's answer must include the word 'Conferees:' with typed/printed names and initials of the two conferees. If the appeal conference indication is missing on answers received by the Board on or after Nov 1, 2000, the Board should return the application to the TC Director for corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation requirement for non-English documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document being relied upon by the examiner is in a language other than English, a translation must be obtained so that the record is clear as to the precise facts relied upon in support of the rejection. The translation may be a machine translation or an English equivalent of the non-English document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The translation should be obtained prior to the appeal conference so participants can consider it. The examiner should reference pertinent portions of the translation at least in the grounds of rejection section of the answer. See MPEP § 706.02 for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of affidavits/declarations/exhibits not entered
rubrics_metrics.description: If an affidavit, declaration, or exhibit was refused entry under 37 CFR 1.116 or prohibited by 37 CFR 41.33, the examiner should not comment on it in the examiner's answer. Likewise, it would be improper for appellant to rely on an affidavit, declaration, or exhibit which was not entered in an appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant has grounds for challenging non-entry of such materials, they should file a timely petition seeking supervisory review of the non-entry. Any affidavits/declarations swearing behind a reference should be clearly identified by the examiner as being considered under 37 CFR 1.131.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's obligation to restate prior Office action rejections fully
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner's answer should not refer, either directly or indirectly, to any prior Office action without fully restating the point relied on in the answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If further explanation of the rejection is necessary, include it in the grounds of rejection set forth in the answer. If a rejected claim were amended after the final rejection by adding limitations, the examiner should address the added limitations in the ground of rejection in the answer. The statement of the rejection in the answer must account for the claim as amended and include rebuttal of arguments presented in the appellant's brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners treat all pending rejected claims as on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are not required to make any determination whether fewer than all of the rejected claims are identified by the appellant as being appealed. If the notice of appeal or appeal brief identifies fewer than all of the rejected claims as being appealed, the issue will be addressed by the Board. Therefore, the examiner will treat all pending, rejected claims as being on appeal, and must maintain all of the rejections set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken, unless appellant has overcome the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In situations where appellant requests to hold a rejection in abeyance or did not present any argument on a rejection in the appeal brief, the examiner should maintain the rejection in the examiner's answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents requirements for examiner's answer — required headings and items
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's answer must include, under appropriate headings in the indicated order: (1) Real Party in Interest; (2) Related Appeals and Interferences; (3) Status of Claims; (4) Status of Amendments After Final; (5) Summary of Claimed Subject Matter; (6) Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal; (7) Claims Appendix; (8) Evidence Relied Upon; (9) Grounds of Rejection (detailed explanations); (10) Response to Argument; (11) Related Proceedings Appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 12.149–12.179.01 should be used as appropriate. Many subitems (see Grounds of Rejection rubric) have detailed statutory-content requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection — 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph (written description/enablement/best mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, the examiner's answer must explain how the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112 is not complied with, including, as appropriate, how the specification and drawings do not describe the subject matter defined by each rejected claim, would not enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the subject matter without undue experimentation (consider factors in MPEP § 2164.01(a)), or do not set forth the best mode contemplated by the appellant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific explanation tied to the specification/drawings and discuss undue experimentation factors where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection — 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph (definiteness)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, the examiner's answer must explain how the claims do not particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which applicant regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain claim language problems and why the claim fails the definiteness requirement with specific references to claim language and, if necessary, specification support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection — 35 U.S.C. 102 (anticipation) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102, the examiner's answer must explain why the rejected claims are anticipated or not patentable under 35 U.S.C. 102, pointing out where all of the specific limitations recited in the rejected claims are found in the prior art relied upon in the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to specific places (page/line/drawing reference) in the prior art showing each limitation is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection — 35 U.S.C. 103 (obviousness) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103, the examiner's answer must: (i) state the ground of rejection and point out where each specific limitation recited in the rejected claims is found in the prior art relied on in the rejection; (ii) identify the differences between the rejected claims and the prior art relied on (i.e., the primary reference); and (iii) explain why it would have been obvious at the time the invention was made to a person of ordinary skill in the art to have modified the primary reference to arrive at the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If questions remain as to how limitations correspond to features in the prior art, the examiner must compare at least one rejected claim feature-by-feature with the prior art, aligning claim language side-by-side with specific page/line/drawing references and quotations as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection — other rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection other than those under 35 U.S.C. 112, 102, or 103, the examiner's answer must specifically explain the basis for the particular rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, specific reasoning for statutory or rule-based rejections outside 112/102/103 so appellant and the Board can understand and review the basis for the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominent identification and approval of new grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must prominently identify (e.g., a separate heading in all capitalized letters) any new ground of rejection that has been approved by the TC Director or designee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the new grounds in both the 'Grounds of Rejection to be Reviewed on Appeal' section and the 'Grounds of Rejection' section, and conclude answers raising new grounds with form paragraph 12.179.01 to notify applicant of response period and include required TC Director/designee approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to appellant's arguments — structure and parity
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must state whether the examiner disagrees with each contention of appellant in the brief with respect to the issues presented and explain reasons for disagreement. The examiner must use headings and subheadings paralleling the headings and subheadings utilized in the appellant's brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address appellant's arguments point-by-point using comparable headings so the Board can readily see the examiner's responses to specific arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence relied upon — listing and citation specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must list the evidence relied on (e.g., patents, publications, admitted prior art) and, for nonpatent references, provide the relevant page(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on prior art, include precise citations (page/line/drawing reference) so claim-to-reference comparisons can be evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs and required form language
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the prescribed form paragraphs (¶ 12.149 through ¶ 12.179.01, as appropriate) for the examiner's answer and cover sheet. Form paragraph language provides the proper headings, notices, and explanatory language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill in bracketed items in form paragraphs (e.g., application number, filing date, appellant name(s), dates) and follow Examiner Notes accompanying form paragraphs for correct usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of examiner answers that raise new legal interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner's answer is believed to contain a new interpretation or application of existing patent law, the answer, application file, and an explanatory memorandum should be forwarded to the TC Director for consideration. If approved by the TC Director, forward to the Office of the Associate Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy for final approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow internal review channels before issuing answers that may effectuate new legal interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to ensure approved amendments are entered in the file before preparing answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Before preparing the answer, the examiner should make certain that all amendments approved for entry have in fact been entered in the file. The Board will return to the TC any application in which approved amendments have not been entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify file wrapper reflect entry of amendments to avoid returns/corrective action by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on citing unpublished decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence with the Board must be on the record. No unpublished decisions which are unavailable to the general public by reason of 35 U.S.C. 122(a) can be cited by the examiner or the appellant except that either may cite an unpublished decision in an application having common ownership with the application on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure citations are publicly available or meet the common-ownership exception; otherwise do not cite unpublished Board/court decisions.
